title: Grade 12 Chemistry — d-Block Elements (Transition Metals)
description: Electronic configuration, properties, and compounds of transition metals
subject: chemistry

questions.question: The d-block elements are those in which the differentiating electron enters the:
questions.explanation: d-block: Groups 3–12, where electrons fill d subshells (3d, 4d, 5d, 6d). Periods 4–7. Most are transition metals (have at least one ion with incomplete d subshell). Zn, Cd, Hg are d-block but NOT transition metals.

questions.question: The electronic configuration of Fe (atomic number 26) is:
questions.explanation: [Ar] = [1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶]. Fe = [Ar] 3d⁶ 4s². Fe²⁺ loses 4s electrons first: [Ar] 3d⁶. Fe³⁺: [Ar] 3d⁵ (half-filled d subshell = extra stability).

questions.question: Transition metals exhibit variable valency (multiple oxidation states) because:
options: Both 3d and 4s electrons can participate in bond formation (close energy levels)
questions.explanation: 3d and 4s subshells are close in energy — electrons from both can be removed. This allows multiple oxidation states. Example: Mn shows +2, +3, +4, +6, +7. Contrast: main group elements have fixed valency.

questions.question: Transition metal compounds are often coloured because:
options: d-d electronic transitions absorb specific wavelengths of visible light (complementary colour observed)
questions.explanation: In transition metal complexes, ligand field splitting splits d orbitals into different energy levels. Electrons absorb visible light to jump between levels (d-d transition). The complementary colour is transmitted/reflected → coloured compound.

questions.question: Which transition metal has the highest melting point?
questions.explanation: Tungsten (W) has the highest melting point of all pure metals: 3422°C. Used in light bulb filaments and welding applications. High MP is due to strong metallic bonding from unpaired d-electrons.

questions.question: Potassium permanganate (KMnO₄) acts as an oxidising agent. The oxidation state of Mn changes from +7 to:
questions.explanation: KMnO₄ in acidic medium: MnO₄⁻ → Mn²⁺ (Mn: +7→+2, gain 5e⁻, purple to colourless). In neutral/alkaline: MnO₄⁻ → MnO₂ (+7→+4, brown precipitate). In strongly alkaline: MnO₄⁻ → MnO₄²⁻ (+7→+6).

questions.question: The anomalous electronic configuration of Cr (Z=24) is [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s¹ (not 3d⁴ 4s²) because:
options: Cr is an exception to the Aufbau principle
Half-filled d subshell (3d⁵) has extra stability due to exchange energy
questions.explanation: Half-filled (3d⁵) and fully-filled (3d¹⁰) d subshells have extra stability (exchange energy). So Cr promotes 1e⁻ from 4s to 3d: [Ar]3d⁵4s¹. Similarly Cu: [Ar]3d¹⁰4s¹ (not 3d⁹4s²).

questions.question: Transition metals are good catalysts because:
options: They have variable oxidation states and can adsorb reactants on their surfaces (heterogeneous catalysis)
questions.explanation: Catalytic activity of transition metals: (1) Variable oxidation states allow them to form intermediate compounds; (2) d-electrons interact with reactants (adsorption); (3) Large surface area in finely divided form. Example: Fe in Haber process, V₂O₅ in Contact process.

questions.question: K₂Cr₂O₇ (potassium dichromate) in acidic solution oxidises. Cr changes from:
questions.explanation: K₂Cr₂O₇: Cr is +6. When it acts as oxidising agent: Cr²O₇²⁻ → 2Cr³⁺ (+6→+3, each Cr gains 3e⁻, total 6e⁻ gained). The orange dichromate solution becomes green (Cr³⁺).

questions.question: Magnetic properties of transition metal ions depend on the number of:
options: Unpaired electrons (more unpaired e⁻ = higher paramagnetism)
questions.explanation: Paramagnetism: due to unpaired electrons (each has a magnetic moment). More unpaired e⁻ = stronger paramagnetism. Example: Fe³⁺ has [Ar]3d⁵ (5 unpaired e⁻) = strongly paramagnetic. Zn²⁺: [Ar]3d¹⁰ (all paired) = diamagnetic.

questions.question: The lanthanide contraction refers to:
options: The large radii of lanthanide elements
The gradual decrease in atomic/ionic radii across the 4f series due to poor shielding of 4f electrons
The shrinkage of f orbitals in compounds
questions.explanation: Lanthanide contraction: as atomic number increases across La-Lu, 4f electrons are added which poorly shield nuclear charge. Size decreases steadily. Consequence: 5d elements have similar radii to 4d counterparts (e.g., Zr/Hf nearly identical size).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of transition metals?
options: Low melting and boiling points (like Na and K)
questions.explanation: Transition metals have HIGH melting and boiling points (due to metallic bonding involving d-electrons), unlike Na/K which melt below 100°C. All other options are correct transition metal characteristics.

questions.question: The IUPAC name of K₂Cr₂O₇ is:
questions.explanation: K₂Cr₂O₇ = potassium dichromate. Orange crystals, strong oxidising agent, used in tanning, electroplating, and organic chemistry. In alkaline conditions: Cr₂O₇²⁻ (dichromate, orange) ⇌ 2CrO₄²⁻ (chromate, yellow).

questions.question: In the Contact Process for making H₂SO₄, the catalyst used is:
questions.explanation: Contact Process: 2SO₂ + O₂ → 2SO₃ (catalyst V₂O₅, 450°C, 1–2 atm). SO₃ + H₂O → H₂SO₄ (via oleum). V₂O₅ works by V⁵⁺/V⁴⁺ redox cycle — variable oxidation state is key.

questions.question: The number of unpaired electrons in Fe²⁺ (with [Ar]3d⁶ configuration) is:
questions.explanation: Fe²⁺: [Ar]3d⁶. d⁶ configuration: filling 5 d orbitals — 4 orbitals get 1e⁻ each, 1 orbital gets 2e⁻ (Hund's rule). Unpaired = 4. (Assuming high-spin, no ligand field splitting.) Magnetic moment ≈ 4.9 BM.
